Title: Boulder City Council Special Meeting - July 13, 2023

Topic1.Title: Declaration for Parks and Recreation Month
Topic1.Summary: Council recognized July as Parks and Recreation Month, presented by Councilmember Joseph. Ali Rhodes from Parks and Recreation highlighted the department's health, environmental, and access programs. Council thanked staff for their work on community green spaces and recreation facilities.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic2.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda, items 2A through 2C, by unanimous vote. No questions or comments were raised on these items. The motion was made and seconded before the vote.

Topic3.Title: New Vista High School Site Development Plan Review
Topic3.Summary: Boulder Valley School District presented a proposed replacement of New Vista High School with a roughly 74,000 square foot two-story building, a new sports field, and updated parking and access. The district described design changes made in response to planning board feedback, including reduced parking, added bike parking, and EV charging. Council members praised the responsiveness and raised questions about the parking lot, geothermal funding, and a multi-use path connection from the east that remains under review.

Topic4.Title: Public Comment on New Vista High School
Topic4.Summary: Molly Sorensen, PTO president at New Vista, urged council to allow the project to proceed quickly because the current building has water damage. She noted the school serves students from mountain communities who rely on driving and emphasized the importance of parking for CU football revenue. Staff confirmed the project should move forward without additional requirements.

Topic5.Title: Concept Plan Review for 4401 Broadway Mixed-Use Project
Topic5.Summary: The applicant proposed a roughly 107,250 square foot mixed-use project including a new home for the Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art, housing, retail, and art studio space. Staff explained that museums are prohibited in the MU2 zone and that the project requires rezoning, land use map changes, and a 29-space parking reduction. Council generally supported the museum use and recommended a North Boulder subcommunity plan update and a flex zone designation.

Topic6.Title: Proposed Unification of Sales Tax Ballot Measures
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented polling results showing strong likely voter support for extending the 0.15 sales tax through 2044 and for a broad set of services. Council discussed a compromise proposal to split the tax 50/50 between the Arts and the general fund, which the petition leaders were open to. Council members debated long-term financial commitments, dedicated funding, and racial equity considerations, and seven members voted to direct staff to prepare an alternative 50/50 ballot measure.

Topic7.Title: Board and Commission Midterm Recruitment Extension
Topic7.Summary: The city clerk reported that 12 vacancies were filled by 12 applications, but several boards received no eligible applicants. Council discussed whether to extend recruitment or wait until the 2024 annual recruitment. Most council members supported waiting until the 2024 recruitment cycle, while a consultant is being brought on to help with future recruitment.
